failureMessage: the precondition is the ONLY decision point — a later-phase skip hides work from the run records and re-litigates a verdict already given

matchLines.what: instructs a conditional skip after the precondition already passed: "{match}"
matchLines.fix: move the run/no-run decision into the task.json precondition, or reword an empty result as an empty outcome; a required input the dispatch lacks is a failure — park the item at task:status:needs-human-action

matchLines.what: code-work announces a discretionary cycle skip: "{match}"
matchLines.fix: let the precondition make that call, or complete the work and report an empty outcome; only a genuine failure may stop a run past the precondition

failureMessage: the merged assertion families no longer accept their pre-merge spelling, and a spelling the engine cannot place is dropped at load — the assertion is simply not there

matchLines.what: {match} is the pre-merge spelling of an index-coverage assertion, which the engine no longer places
matchLines.fix: restate it as a named `extractValueSets` entry quantified over by `requireIndexCoverage`'s `eachValueOfSet` — the normalizer that rewrote it retired in #1643

matchLines.what: {match} is the pre-merge spelling of an index-coverage assertion, which the engine no longer places
matchLines.fix: restate it as a `requireIndexCoverage` entry — `listFile`/`globFile` become `indexFile`, `asText` becomes `coveredByText`, `globLineMatching` becomes `coveredByGlobLinesMatching`, and the defaults the old keys implied (`whenIndexFileAbsent`, `anchorFindingsAt`) are now declared

matchLines.what: {match} is the pre-merge spelling of a parsed-document assertion, which the engine no longer places
matchLines.fix: restate it as a `checkParsedFiles` entry — one selector (`file`, or `filesMatching` + `whereFileContains`) carrying `forEachEntryAtField`/`whereEntryFieldEquals` or `requireEqualFields`

failureMessage: the doc pointer is the More line a finding prints, and nothing opens it until the check fires — a stale one sits broken until a session follows it into nothing

checkSetValues.what: doc: names {value}, which is not a path in this tree
checkSetValues.fix: point doc: at the file that owns the rule's depth, repo-relative (a canon pack's under packs/<pack>/), or drop the field

failureMessage: a check nobody watched fail meets its first false positive in a member's Stop hook, where every session pays for it
fix: write the fixture first — a violating tree must find and a clean one must not — and land it in the same change

requireCoChange.what: {path} declares a new check, and no test file changed with it
{path} adds a rule, and no test file changed with it
